chapter: Erroll Garner, the 1952 arrest and Florida
title: The end of jazz on 52nd Street and the opening of Birdland
summary: The clubs became girlie shows as 52nd Street was cleared; Royal Roost and Birdland followed.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, around that time, they were trying to get rid of 52nd Street as Tin Pan Alley, you know. And they were going to tear all of those structures down and rebuild, supposedly, in order to get the musicians out of there. And as soon as the clubs closed from playing jazz they made all of
Well, that's what had been along most of 52nd Street at that point.
Uh-huh. So they ran everybody off of 52nd Street like that, and so just luckily, they opened Birdland.
Well, Royal Roost was the first one over there.
